title: LSASS memory access with full-access masks by PowerShell on scranton
rationale: All describe the same action: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976) on scranton.dmevals.local opened lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff at 2020-05-02T03:05:16Z (plus the 4663 audit record of the same handle open). F10/F34 also include the nashua wsmprovhost LSASS open, but the dominant shared action is the scranton LSASS full-access open, which best fits T1003.001 (LSASS Memory).

title: PowerShell LSASS full-access open during hands-on-keyboard intrusion (T1212 framing)
rationale: Describes wsmprovhost.exe on nashua opening lsass.exe with 0x1F3FFF; the observed action is LSASS memory access, best fit T1003.001 (finding itself notes no dump payload observed, hence suspicious).

title: No Kerberos ticket theft/forgery; LSASS handle access by PowerShell on scranton
rationale: Finding reports no ticket theft/forgery; the only credential-access-shaped action is PowerShell opening lsass.exe with full-access masks on scranton, T1003.001.

title: No SAML token forgery; LSASS access by PowerShell/wsmprovhost
rationale: Finding reports no SAML/token artifacts; the observed credential-material theft is LSASS full-access access by PowerShell/wsmprovhost, T1003.001.

title: Keystroke-Check AV-evasion function and remote keylogger deployment to nashua
rationale: Describes the Keystroke-Check function and Get-Keystrokes keylogger deployment; the credential-access action is keylogging, T1056.001.

title: WebDAV/UNC forced-authentication exfil path from scranton to 192.168.0.4
rationale: Describes the Invoke-Exfil WebDAV/UNC path with explicit credentials and the powershell.exe connection to 192.168.0.4; the credential-access-relevant action is forced authentication via UNC/WebDAV, T1187.

title: Credential-access tooling staged on scranton (Sysinternals, keylogger, exfil scripts)
rationale: Both describe the staging and running of the Sysinternals toolset (accesschk, PsExec64, sdelete64) and credential/exfil scripts from C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite on scranton; the shared action is staging unsecured credential-access tooling, best fit T1552.

title: Attacker tooling staged in C:\Windows\Temp on nashua
rationale: Describes staging of python.exe, Rar.exe, sdelete64.exe in C:\Windows\Temp on nashua; unsecured credential-access tooling staging, T1552.

title: Credential-named file harvesting and archiving on scranton and nashua
rationale: Both describe enumeration of credential-named files (*psw*, *pass*, *login*, *admin*, *vpn) and archiving to Draft.Zip/working.zip on scranton and nashua; credentials in files, T1552.001.

title: accesschk.exe creating passwordsDB in SysinternalsSuite directory
rationale: Describes accesschk.exe creating a 'passwordsDB' file; credential material in files, T1552.001.

title: Cleartext pbeesly password on PsExec64 command lines to NASHUA
rationale: Describes cleartext credentials in PsExec64 command lines; credentials in files/command lines, T1552.001.

title: Get-PrivateKeys certificate private-key export to .pfx on scranton
rationale: All describe the same Get-PrivateKeys/Export-PfxCertificate action exporting cert:\LocalMachine private keys to a password-protected .pfx on scranton; private keys, T1552.004.

title: No password spraying; valid pbeesly credentials reused via PsExec64 to NASHUA
rationale: Finding explicitly reports no spraying; the observed action is credential reuse with PsExec to NASHUA, i.e. lateral movement (SMB/Windows Admin Shares), out of scope.

title: Credential-theft campaign on scranton with lateral SMB/PsExec movement to nashua
rationale: Finding reports no AiTM positioning; the described action spans credential theft plus lateral SMB/PsExec movement to nashua, whose best single fit is lateral movement, out of scope.

title: csc.exe compiling attacker .NET payloads from PowerShell response files
rationale: Describes csc.exe compiling attacker .NET payloads; this is execution (compile after delivery), out of scope.

title: No MFA interception; PowerShell Remoting logon-session enumeration on nashua
rationale: Finding reports no MFA interception artifacts; the observed action is PowerShell Remoting execution/enumeration by pbeesly on nashua, out of scope.

title: Screen-saver payload in C:\ProgramData\victim launched on scranton
rationale: Describes a malicious .scr screen saver executed by explorer spawning a PowerShell stager; this is execution/persistence, out of scope.

title: sdclt.exe execution proxy before payload compilation
rationale: Describes sdclt.exe execution proxy preceding payload compilation; this is execution/defense evasion, out of scope.

title: hostui.exe elevation attempt and registry-stored encoded PowerShell stager
rationale: Describes UAC bypass via hostui.exe runas and registry-stored encoded PowerShell stager; this is privilege escalation/execution, out of scope.
